title: The USO show format and rehearsals at Noll Studios
summary: The thirteen-person show ran an hour with an MC, three women and an eight-piece band, rehearsed at Noll Studios.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: To the USO. So I'm rehearsing with Jesse Stone every day. And there would be different units in the billing where we was rehearsing that. We was rehearsing at Noll Studios downtown on 52nd Street, I think...51st and Broadway. We rehearsed there. And there was a lot of bands rehearsing in there for different things. Well, that was takin' up my day. I mean, it was nice. I'd go down there. But after you get the show down letter-perfect, which the show only...it only run an hour... And after you get the show down letter-perfect, you still had to rehearse, you know....
Now, this was what kind of show? This had what kind of acts?
Let me see. We had an MC, a Master of Ceremonies. There was only 13 people in the show, which consisted of three girls... There was three girls in the
show, two of them danced together. One of them was Jesse Stone's wife, one of the girl dancers. The other girl, Gwen Tines(?), she was a vocalist. She was from Canada. She was a very good vocalist.
The MC, three girls, four... I think the band had seven or eight pieces in it. And we had a manager. Sylvester Lewis was the manager. He was an ex-trumpet player at the time.
He had been with Claude Hopkins.

Claude Hopkins. He'd been with a lot of different bands around. And he was the manager of the show, and he turned out to be a very good manager, too. I mean, I was actually surprised. Well, he had did it before. He managed a big show, a big USO show over in Europe. That was before he come with us. And he was very successful with it. They thought the world of Mr. Lewis.
So anyway, all together, intact, we had thirteen people, including the three women.
